expectations.text: An invalid granularity (e.g., --since 1z) is treated as a literal string by parseRelativeSince (returns the string unchanged), and parsePythonIsoformat then fails it, so the script either errors with a non-zero exit and a human-readable message OR returns total_events=0 with an explicit warning — silent fallback to 'no filter' is a failure
expectations.evidence: Command: node event_logger.js stats --wiki-root <work> --since 1z. exit=2 (non-zero). stderr: `[event_logger] error: --since value "1z" is not a valid relative duration (e.g. 7d, 24h, 15m) or absolute ISO timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD...)`. No stdout was emitted, so there is no silent fallback — the CLI rejects the input at the boundary (event_logger.ts:563-574).

expectations.text: Absolute ISO timestamp with +00:00 UTC offset is accepted identically to its Z-suffix equivalent — re-running the third command with the same wall-clock cutoff but rendered as `<ABS_ISO_10D>+00:00` instead of `<ABS_ISO_10D>Z` produces the same total_events=5
expectations.evidence: Cmd3 (--since 2026-04-23T19:34:21Z): total_ops=5, ops_by_type={fix:1, lint:1, ingest:2, query:1}. Cmd4 (--since 2026-04-23T19:34:21+00:00): total_ops=5, ops_by_type={fix:1, lint:1, ingest:2, query:1}. eval_feedback.overall: All 7 expectations pass cleanly under the rewritten dynamic-cutoff prompt. The previously-failing expectation #2 (--since 30d → 9 events) and expectation #3 (--since <ABS_ISO_10D_Z> → 5 events) now both pass: with the cutoff computed as now-10d off the fixture's own now(), the abs-ISO threshold reliably falls between the 5-day cohort (after cutoff) and 20-day cohort (before cutoff), so the partition is stable. The Z-vs-+00:00 equivalence also holds. Note: the script's JSON uses the field name `total_ops` rather than `total_events` — count semantics match the eval expectations one-for-one.
